nodes.description: Private uint256 secretNumber holding the winning number; written in shuffle() using weak randomness and compared in play().
Public uint256 lastPlayed storing the timestamp (now) of the last play; used in kill() cooldown check.
Public uint256 betPrice = 0.001 ether, the minimum value accepted by play().
Public address ownerAddr set to msg.sender in the constructor; authorization anchor for kill().
Public Game[] gamesPlayed array; each play() pushes a Game struct record.
constructor() sets ownerAddr = msg.sender and calls shuffle() to seed secretNumber.
internal shuffle() computes secretNumber = uint8(sha3(now, block.blockhash(block.number-1))) % 10 + 1 (weak randomness).
payable public play(uint256 number) validates betPrice, records the Game, transfers the whole balance to the winner, then updates lastPlayed.
public kill() allows ownerAddr to suicide(msg.sender) after 6 hours since lastPlayed.
Anonymous payable fallback function that accepts plain ether transfers.
msg.sender: caller-controlled address used as owner, player and transfer recipient.
block.timestamp (now): miner-influenceable time source used for randomness seeding, lastPlayed and kill() cooldown.
msg.sender.transfer(this.balance) in play(): external call sending the full contract balance to an untrusted address before lastPlayed is updated.
suicide(msg.sender) in kill(): self-destruct transferring remaining balance, guarded only by owner check and timestamp window.
secretNumber = uint8(sha3(now, block.blockhash(block.number-1))) % 10 + 1: predictable on-chain randomness derived from timestamp and block hash.
lastPlayed = now in play(): timestamp-dependent state update affecting kill() authorization window.
Parameter number of play(uint256 number): attacker-supplied guess between 1 and 10.
Local Game game struct built in play() from msg.sender and number before being pushed to gamesPlayed.

edges.reason: msg.sender is assigned to ownerAddr in the constructor, setting the privileged owner.
constructor() calls shuffle() to initialize secretNumber.
block.timestamp (now) feeds sha3 used to derive the secret number, making randomness miner/timestamp dependent.
Weak-randomness result is written into secretNumber, the value players must guess.
play() receives the caller-supplied guess as parameter number.
msg.sender is stored as game.player in the local Game struct.
Parameter number is stored as game.number in the local Game struct.
The local Game struct is pushed into the gamesPlayed array.
secretNumber is read in play() for the winning comparison (number == secretNumber).
betPrice is read in play() require to enforce the minimum bet.
play() reaches the balance transfer branch when the guess matches secretNumber.
msg.sender is the recipient of the external transfer(this.balance) call, an attacker-controlled address.
The external transfer to msg.sender can re-enter play() (or the payable fallback) before lastPlayed is updated, enabling repeated balance draining.
play() writes lastPlayed after the transfer logic executes.
block.timestamp (now) is assigned to lastPlayed, a miner-influenceable value controlling later authorization.
kill() executes suicide(msg.sender), an owner-only destructive operation.
ownerAddr is the stored privileged address compared inside kill()'s access check.
msg.sender is checked against ownerAddr to authorize kill().
lastPlayed participates in kill()'s time-window access condition (now > lastPlayed + 6 hours).
block.timestamp (now) is used in kill()'s cooldown condition, making the authorization window timestamp dependent.

normalization_plan.reason: Play()'s number parameter is only meaningful as the guess argument consumed by play(); it should be folded into the play function node.
